evidence.title: Limitations of zT as a figure of merit for nanostructured thermoelectric materials

novelty_basis: The single passage frames the work entirely as numerical simulation of measurements "as they would be done experimentally" and of an idealised cooler, but nowhere notes that experimental corroboration is absent, needed, or planned, and offers no measured comparison. Simulating an experimental protocol is not a substitute for the experiment, and no convention in the passage makes the check unnecessary, so the missing validation is unacknowledged rather than explained away.
statement: The dependence of thermal conductivity on nanoparticle density in nanostructured thermoelectric material rests on a single numerical study that simulates how such measurements would be performed, with no accompanying experimental measurement to confirm the simulated dependence (and no direction or magnitude reported).

evidence.title: Limitations of zT as a figure of merit for nanostructured thermoelectric materials

novelty_basis: The single exposed passage describes only a simulation study that mimics how measurements "would be done experimentally"; it never states or acknowledges that the grain-size dependence of electrical conductivity lacks experimental validation, and no passage flags this as an open question. The supporting relation carries method 'simulation', experimental_confirmation false, direction 'unclear', and n_sources 1, so nothing in the evidence recognises the gap.
statement: The dependence of electrical conductivity on average grain size in nanostructured thermoelectric materials is supported here only by numerical simulation from a single source, with no experimental confirmation and no stated direction of the effect, leaving the simulated grain-size trend unvalidated against measured samples.
